description: Tests for structurally malformed records. Robustness category H.

source_records.text: TEST FIXTURE: Subject observed at Test Location AA. No record ID present.

fixtures.expected_behavior: JSONFileConnector uses row['record_id'] which raises KeyError. Or if using .get(), record_id would be None. The pipeline may fail or assign None as record_id.
fixtures.rationale: JSONFileConnector accesses row['record_id'] directly without .get() fallback. Missing record_id raises KeyError in the connector.
fixtures.weakness_description: Records missing the record_id field cause a KeyError in JSONFileConnector.fetch() because it uses direct dict access (row['record_id']). A production system must validate required fields before ingestion and assign a deterministic ID (hash of content + source + date) to records missing an ID.

fixtures.input_condition: Record with extra unknown fields not in the schema

source_records.text: TEST FIXTURE: Subject Eta observed at Test Location BB.

fixtures.expected_behavior: Pipeline ignores unknown fields. JSONFileConnector only reads record_id, source, date, text. Extra fields are silently discarded.
fixtures.rationale: JSONFileConnector uses explicit key access for known fields only. Unknown keys in the row dict are never accessed.

fixtures.input_condition: Record with numeric (integer) record_id instead of string

source_records.text: TEST FIXTURE: Subject Theta observed at Test Location CC.

fixtures.expected_behavior: record_id is passed directly as integer to Record dataclass. Deduplication set comparison works (int 9001 vs int 9001 is equal). Record is ingested with integer ID.
fixtures.rationale: Python set membership check works for integers. The Record dataclass does not enforce string type for record_id. Numeric IDs pass through without error.
